summary.headline: BCL Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore (10.5% margin) despite revenue falling to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue fell to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore, mainly due to closure of the edible oil unit and exit from packaged oil. EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore, with margin up 370 bps to 10.5%, and PAT rose 6% to INR 36 crore (5.7% margin). Distillery EBITDA margin improved to 12.41%, while ENA realisations fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. A fire at a 200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol tank on 19 June 2026 shut that plant temporarily; management said insurance recovery is virtually certain and no net loss was booked. Management also completed the acquisition of the remaining 25% of Svaksha Distillery and reduced working capital borrowings, but deferred the Fatehabad 250 KLPD project and the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project.

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 12.41% in Q1 FY27 versus 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26. ENA volume rose to 19,376 KL from 7,960 KL YoY, but ENA realisation fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. The 115 TPH paddy straw boiler meets 100% of steam and power needs.

segments.name: Country liquor (PML)
segments.commentary: Sold 6,37,993 boxes, up 42% QoQ and 46% YoY. Punjab Raspberry launched in Q4 FY26 and Jamun Vodka in July 2026. Management targets 30 lakh cases this year out of a market of about 1.25 crore cases per annum in Punjab.

segments.name: Edible oil / packaged oil (exited)
segments.commentary: Exit completed, including closure of the Bathinda oil and vanaspati unit. Soft oil refinery and trading continue as legacy operations. Revenue decline was mainly from this exit.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the 200 KLPD Bathinda plant to restart in about 15 days from the call, and that the new 150 KLPD Bathinda unit (commissioned in early July 2026) will substantially offset the lost volume.
Order book described as full for about the next three months, supported by OMC allocation of about 4.5 crore litres from a Supreme Court order covering until November.
Management guided to a sustained distillery/overall margin range of about 10% to 12%, while noting raw material and fuel price volatility.
Working capital limit to be reduced by INR 50 crore in August 2026; management aims to bring working capital utilisation towards zero over about 1.5 years.
No share buyback planned for now. Debt will rise only if a new capex project is started.
capex_capacity: Svaksha Distillery (350 KLPD, Kharagpur, West Bengal) became wholly owned on 30 June 2026 after the remaining 25% stake was acquired.
Newly added 150 KLPD Bathinda unit began commercial trials at end-June 2026 and was commissioned in the first half of July 2026.
200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol plant shut after the 19 June 2026 fire; the tank was holding about 90,000 litres at the time and is under repair.
Fatehabad 250 KLPD grain-based plant: orders and advances are on hold after social media backlash; machinery orders are reportedly finalised and management is waiting before starting construction.
Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project is on hold because biodiesel prices are not remunerative. Goyal Distillery 250 KLPD project is on hold pending industry clarity.
Malt plant is at conceptualisation stage with no timeline. IMFL entry targeted for next year, with the company still working on it.
Bio-CBG is under active evaluation (Haryana policy noted), with paddy straw feedstock seen as tricky. The company is not making biodiesel.
demand_pricing: ENA and private ethanol supply face price pressure from oversupply. Average private ethanol price is about INR 58/litre ex-factory, mainly to Reliance.

Management said maize-based ethanol to OMCs is profitable, while FCI-rice-based ethanol is near cost. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same. Blended average EBITDA is about 12%, roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA.
Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter. Current maize price is about INR 25/kg, and management said ENA prices have been revised upwards.
DDGS prices have eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for both maize and rice based.
Management expects ethanol demand to improve only slightly next year, as sugarcane-based ethanol is unlikely to be allowed. Flex fuel demand is a long-term driver, with few FFV models on sale so far.
Management said E20 is in place for about 18 months with no major vehicle damage seen, but blending expansion beyond E20 may be delayed. Isobutanol and SAF are cited as future demand sources.

qa_highlights.question: At what price is ethanol sold to private players, and is it FCI rice or maize based?
qa_highlights.answer: Private ethanol buyers are mainly Reliance at an average ex-factory price of about INR 58/litre. Private buyers use damaged grain, while the company's own FCI-rice ethanol is tied to 40% of OMC allocation. Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Cause of the Bathinda fire and safeguards for other plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the likely cause was static charge, possibly from clothing of a nearby worker. The company has added facilities to prevent such incidents and called it rare.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for grain ethanol after E20 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is expected to improve only slightly next year because sugarcane ethanol is unlikely to be allowed. Flex fuel is a long-term driver, with isobutanol and SAF as additional sources, and cooking fuel use was also cited.

qa_highlights.question: Unit economics across FCI-rice, OMC maize and ENA/private ethanol?
qa_highlights.answer: FCI-rice ethanol to OMCs is near cost. Maize-based ethanol to OMCs is quite profitable. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same, with blended EBITDA margin near 12%, or roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA on average.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Goyal bio-CNG, biodiesel and the 250 KLPD Goyal Distillery project?
qa_highlights.answer: Bio-CNG is under active evaluation after a favourable new policy, though paddy straw is tricky, mainly due to by-product sale. The company is not making biodiesel. The 250 KLPD Goyal project is on hold pending industry clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project on hold, and does maize oil locally sourced change this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said biodiesel prices are not remunerative and biodiesel feedstock is largely imported, so government has focused less on it. Isobutanol is being tested to promote indigenous feedstock. Management said the government's view could not be commented on.

qa_highlights.question: Malt plant and IMFL entry timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Malt plant is still at conceptualisation with no timeline. IMFL entry is being worked on and is hoped for next year. Management views country liquor as more profitable than competitive IMFL.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the 250 KLPD Fatehabad project after the July statement about construction by August?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders and advances are on hold after social media backlash against the ethanol policy. Machinery orders are finalised and the company is waiting before starting construction.

qa_highlights.question: Land sale timing, debt repayment and release of pledged shares?
qa_highlights.answer: No update on the land sale, as Bathinda real estate is slow and there is no rush. Working capital utilisation is low, some small loans were repaid, and banks released pledged shares. Working capital limit to be cut by INR 50 crore in August.

qa_highlights.question: Trend in DDGS realisations and Punjab country liquor market share?
qa_highlights.answer: DDGS prices eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for maize and rice based. Punjab country liquor market is about 1.25 crore cases a year, with a 30 lakh case target for this year.

qa_highlights.question: Volume outlook, total debt level and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes should stay about flat until the 200 KLPD unit restarts in about 15 days. Working capital utilisation is about INR 60 crore, with total debt around INR 360 crore including working capital. Debt rises only with a new capex project, and working capital is to be run towards zero over about 1.5 years. No buyback is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol mixing in diesel, E20 damage, and government mandates beyond E20?
qa_highlights.answer: Management distinguished ethanol-in-diesel, which faces a flash point issue, from isobutanol, which it said is still under trial and not shelved. It said E20 has run 18 months without major vehicle damage, but further blending could be delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Insurance cover and stock lost in the 200 KL tank, and expected restart?
qa_highlights.answer: The tank held about 90,000 litres at the time. The plant is being repaired and is expected to restart in about 15 days. Management said both stock loss and profit loss are covered by insurance, and the P&L impact is still being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Share of the Supreme Court-allowed OMC volume and the order book outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is among the biggest gainers, with about 4.5 crore litres from both units under the Supreme Court order, covering until November. The order book is more than full for the next 3 months. Flex fuel demand will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Current maize price, margin outlook and state subsidy for CBG?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize is about INR 25/kg now. ENA prices have been revised upwards, but raw material and fuel costs are rising. Management guided margins at about 10-12% with variation. Haryana has a CBG policy and the central policy is also favourable.

risks_watch: Restart timing and insurance recovery for the 200 KLPD Bathinda plant, which was shut after the 19 June 2026 fire; P&L impact still under evaluation.
ENA and private ethanol price pressure from oversupply (ENA realisation INR 58/litre vs INR 70/litre), against rising maize (about INR 25/kg) and fuel costs.
Policy uncertainty on ethanol demand: blending beyond E20 may be delayed, sugarcane ethanol unlikely to be allowed, and flex fuel vehicle availability is minimal with one model on sale.
Order book depends on the one-time Supreme Court-linked OMC allocation (about 4.5 crore litres) which runs only until November; no visibility beyond that.
Deferred growth projects (Fatehabad 250 KLPD, Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel, Goyal 250 KLPD) and IMFL/malt plans with no timelines; watch for any restart decisions.
Working capital reduction (INR 50 crore cut in August) and debt trajectory towards zero working capital use over about 1.5 years; land sale in Bathinda has no timeline.
key_quotes: I want to reassure investors that based on our assessment, full recovery of the resulting losses through insurance claims is considered virtually certain and no net financial loss has been recognized in this result.
So, prices for biodiesel are very, very low. So that's why.
No, I don't want to create any false hope for you.
So I think in the coming months, we'll see quite a few launches of flex fuel vehicles, and we'll see E87 being available at even more pumps.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on financial recovery, debt reduction and insurance cover, but cautious and non-committal on policy outcomes such as flex fuel, E27, biodiesel pricing, the Fatehabad project and the land sale. It repeatedly declined to give timelines or forecasts beyond the next few months.
